name: Generate Song
description: Makes a song from a description and, optionally, lyrics on a music model. The tempo, key and time signature are for you to set or for the model to choose.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.label: Description
inputs.description: The style, mood, instruments and tempo of the song.

inputs.name: lyrics
inputs.label: Lyrics
inputs.description: Sung as written, with [verse] and [chorus] lines to part it. Empty: the model writes them.

inputs.name: instrumental
inputs.label: Instrumental
inputs.description: No singing. The lyrics are ignored.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.label: Style reference
inputs.description: A recording whose voice and timbre the song takes. Optional.

inputs.name: language
inputs.label: Language
inputs.description: The language sung, by its code (en, fr, pt, ja).

inputs.name: bpm
inputs.label: Tempo (BPM)
inputs.description: Beats a minute. 0: the model chooses.

inputs.name: key
inputs.label: Key
inputs.description: For example C major or F# minor. Empty: the model chooses.

inputs.name: time_signature
inputs.label: Time signature
inputs.description: Beats to the bar: 4 is 4/4, 3 is 3/4. Empty: the model chooses.

inputs.name: creativity
inputs.label: Creativity
inputs.description: How freely the model that writes the song picks its ideas. Lower is steadier. Unset: the model's own (0.85).

inputs.name: keep_description
inputs.label: Keep my description
inputs.description: Use the description exactly as written. Otherwise the model first rewrites it with more detail.

inputs.name: quality
inputs.label: Quality
inputs.description: The file the model makes: mp3 (128 kb/s), mp3-320 (320 kb/s) or lossless (a 24-bit WAV, nothing lost to compression).

inputs.name: adapter
inputs.label: Adapter
inputs.description: A singer or style adapter (LoRA) from the music server's adapters folder. Unset: none. Changing it makes the server reload the model, which takes a moment.

inputs.name: adapter_scale
inputs.label: Adapter strength
inputs.description: How strongly the adapter is applied. 1 is as it was trained; lower is subtler.
